findings.fix: Each name tier is now TWO passes in `scope_tiers`: `exact=True` first, `_whole_string` (anchored, case-insensitive) only if the exact pass finds nothing. `_resolve_in` threads a per-pass `fold` label through every return, so a folded resolution records `narrowed: name-case-folded` in the step's trace note.
findings.why_this_fix: The reviewer offered a code guard OR a documentation correction. A guard that raises on ambiguity before `index`/`near` is wrong — those two keys exist precisely to select among N matches, so gating them on uniqueness would break M6 and M38 outright. A documentation-only fix would have shipped a case pinning the wrong-element pick as correct. Ordering is the third option and the smallest: it restores base behaviour exactly wherever an exact-case match exists (which is every page in the suite), reaches the fold only where nothing else matches, and makes the fold visible. It also fixes the `extract_all` growth the review measured, at the same line.

findings.fix: `resolve_advertised` is now a COUNT identity: for each (role, name) the observation advertises k times, `resolve(..., many=True)` must reach k elements. It also takes `"*"` (every role in the observation) plus an explicit `resolve_advertised_except` list, and the case now uses `["*"]` with two named exceptions instead of grading one role.
findings.why_not_handle_identity: `observe()` returns {role, name} dicts and holds no element handle to compare against, so handle identity is not available without changing what `observe` returns — a change to the planner's input, for an eval-side check. The count is a proxy and its ceiling is stated in the code and in the case: k elements could still be the wrong k.
findings.may_narrow_kept_false: Rejected the acceptance's third clause deliberately. The reviewer asked that `task`/`action` match what the executor would pass, which would set `may_narrow=True` for `extract`. A narrowing is a RECOVERY; an invariant that only holds after one is not the invariant this case claims. Stated in the code comment.
findings.red_first: Demonstration, not a shipped case: a host page with `<button id=HOST-BTN>Continue</button>` and an iframe holding `<button id=INNER-BTN>Continue</button>`. observe() advertises {('button','Continue'): 2}. OLD check: `no raise -> passed`. NEW check: `ResolveError: {'role': 'button', 'name': 'Continue'} matches in 2 separate documents (the page and 1 frame(s))` -> RED. Not committed as a case because main-frame-first tier construction is ADR-028's deliberate design, so such a case could never go green.
findings.second_defect_found_here: Widening to every role immediately reddened on our own inspector: `Locator.count: InvalidSelectorError: Error while parsing selector `button[name=/^\s*UPLOAD\s+A\s+FILING\s+\(\.HTM\s+/\s+\.HTML\s+/\s+\.TXT\)\s*$/i]` - unexpected symbol "\" at position 50`. Playwright serialises the pattern into a `/…/flags` selector literal and a bare `/` in the name terminates it — a page-content-dependent crash that `classify` reads as `act`, i.e. R6's failure mode reached by a different route. `_whole_string` now escapes `/`. This was a live defect in the T-M42-20 fix that the review did not find and the widened check did.
findings.exclusions: `button` and `WebArea`, both named in the case with reasons. `WebArea` is Chromium's document root, not an addressable ARIA role. `button` is a genuine role-level engine disagreement (see T-M42-20-D4) and is declared in docs/support-matrix.md D32.

findings.fix: `_whole_string` raises `ResolveError("element-not-found", ...)` on a non-string, which `agent.classify` reads as `locate`. Refused there because both tiers route through it.
findings.red_first: resolver-non-string-target-is-a-locate-failure: on fbe304b `failure:act` — `step 2 (extract): AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'split'`. Expected `failure:locate`.
findings.alternative_not_taken: A `task`-class plan refusal in the shape `unsupported target key(s)` uses is the stronger fix — a non-string name is a bad PLAN, not an absent element — but it means teaching `plan_gap` about value types, a wider change than this repair. The acceptance allows either; `locate` restores base behaviour exactly.
